summary: Create one PTY; command is sent once to its shell, or --agent starts a provider
usage: corral terminal create [--worktree VALUE] [--title VALUE] [--command VALUE] [--agent claude|codex|grok] [--model VALUE] [--effort VALUE] [--advisor VALUE] [--prompt VALUE] [--prompt-file VALUE] [--focus] [--request-id VALUE] [--help] [--json] [--timeout-ms VALUE] [--socket VALUE] [--instance VALUE]
examples: corral terminal create --worktree current --agent claude --model opus --effort high --prompt "review the diff" --timeout-ms 600000 --json
notes: Local macOS terminal backend guard v1 required (app/scripts/build-terminal-backend.sh); no automatic fallback to unguarded effects.
Handles bind profile, backend boot and PTY generation; runtime restart preserves handles when backend survives. Handles are not dispatch authorization.
Process conditions are unsupported and rejected without effects; general send targets current foreground.
Raw retention: last 1048576 bytes per PTY, backend lifetime; cursor is byte offset plus UTF-8 decoder carry. bytesBase64 is lossless; text is decoded UTF-8.
Read limit: 1..262144 bytes; screen limit: 1..262144 UTF-8 bytes; list limit: 1..10000. Input/command max 65536 UTF-8 bytes, title max 1024 bytes. NUL rejected.
Ready means transport, send means backend accepted, neither means application consumption or task completion. Close exitCode is null.

Request IDs: r1.<13-digit Unix milliseconds>.<UUID>, mint immediately before a new create/send; CLI mints if omitted. Retention 24 hours/10000 receipts; missing receipt for an admitted/older request or a pending receipt is unknown, never re-executed; lost results still count toward this runtime’s capacity. A refusal that reports outcome not_started never began the effect, so it leaves its --request-id unspent: send the same id again and it is admitted.
Headless supports all commands except switch/focus and create --focus. Rename applies to every pane in the tab.

Agents (LIFE-394): terminal create --agent claude|codex|grok starts a managed provider in the new PTY. --model/--effort/--advisor/--prompt/--prompt-file require --agent; --command and --agent are mutually exclusive; --prompt and --prompt-file are mutually exclusive; --advisor applies to --agent claude only. Rejections are effect-free invalid_request.

Agent ready means two observations 750 ms apart that are all idle or done, interactive_ready and not launch-pending and that share one state_change_seq, AND the guard reporting the expected bundled detect manifest for that provider. done is idle whose completion was not seen: on a completion transition herdr sets seen to is_active_tab && outer_terminal_focus != Some(false), so a pane that is not the active tab, or whose window focus is explicitly false, reports done at the end of every turn it finishes — that is GUI attention, not readiness, so both count. wait --for agent-ready and --for agent-idle run that one predicate; they differ in when they are asked and about what. A blocked screen and an unverified detect manifest both return satisfied false immediately, with the reason in agent.evidence, instead of waiting for the deadline. phase is never reported as ready while that gate does not currently hold, whatever the reason — unverified manifest, a working frame, a moved state_change_seq, a single sample — even if a ready was stored earlier; such a pane reports launching, and agent.evidence.samples and agent.evidence.detectManifest say which it was.

corral reads only the session record it can prove this pane owns: the minted session id for claude and grok, and for codex the single rollout whose session_meta cwd is this directory and whose timestamp is at or after the launch. With no such rollout, or more than one, the match count, resolvedModel and record.path are all unknown rather than read from another session's file.

Prompt submission is fail-closed and effect-free when refused: detect_manifest_unverified when the guard's active detect manifest is not the expected bundled one, agent_blocked on a blocking screen, agent_not_ready when the ready gate or the compare-and-submit state_change_seq check fails, prompt_already_delivered when the provider record already holds the body.

A prompt without --wait is queued, not completed: herdr acknowledges the queue and corral has not seen the body in the provider record yet. Delivery and the wait are reported separately. record.matchCount/unavailableReason answer delivery: exactly one match inside the submission window (submit second floored, after the pre-submit cursor, and the cursor's prefix digest unchanged) confirms it and sets stage confirmed and phase accepted. wait.requested/satisfied/reason answer the wait: --wait accepted is satisfied by that confirmation, and --wait responded additionally needs a working turn observed within this submission and an assistant record after the match, closed by the same two-observation idle gate. A deadline, a blocking screen or an exit ends the wait unsatisfied with wait.reason deadline|agent_blocked|agent_exited. outcome is completed only for a satisfied wait; anything else is outcome unknown and is never re-submitted automatically, and the confirmed delivery is still reported.

create --prompt submits once at ready. If a blocker appears first the create ends there, complete, and does not hold the prompt — resume with terminal prompt under its own request id. The prompt stage of a create files its own receipt under the derived id r1.<create milliseconds>.<sha256("<create id>|prompt") first 16 bytes as a UUID>, and the receipt hash covers the body, so the same id with different content is request_conflict — unless that stage was refused before it began, which leaves the id unspent and admits the corrected body.
